content: The absorption of tetracyclines can be impaired by multivalent cation-containing products, potentially reducing their efficacy. It is recommended to administer tetracyclines separately from such products. Sodium citrate or citric acid can reduce the levels of pamidronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Dosing should be separated by at least 2 hours, and caution is advised with monitoring. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of penbutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral formulations. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies exclusively to oral forms. Separate dosing by 2 hours and monitor carefully. Sodium citrate or citric acid diminishes the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of pindolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction is specific to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the level or effect of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the level or effect of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is relevant only for oral formulations. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the levels of propranolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies exclusively to oral forms. Separate dosing by 2 hours and monitor carefully. Sodium citrate or citric acid increases the level or effect of pseudoephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid diminishes the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Sodium citrate or citric acid increases the level or effect of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Elevated plasma levels of quinidine may occur, potentially leading to cardiac conduction disturbances and arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of risedronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the level or effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is specific to oral forms. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies exclusively to oral forms. Separate dosing by 2 hours and monitor carefully. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the level or effect of sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their efficacy. Administer tetracyclines separately from these products. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of sotalol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral formulations. Separate dosing by 2 hours and monitor carefully. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of timolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies exclusively to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid diminishes the effects of trandolapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Sodium citrate or citric acid reduces the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate dosing by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with aspirin through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. At moderate doses, salicylate levels increase, while at high doses, salicylate levels decrease due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with aspirin rectal formulations through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with balsalazide through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Blessed thistle reduces the effects of sodium citrate or citric acid through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and its clinical significance is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with choline magnesium trisalicylate through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of chromium by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Devil's claw reduces the effects of sodium citrate or citric acid through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with diflunisal through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with mesalamine through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with non-ASA salicylates through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with salsalate through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of strontium ranelate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours when possible and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with sulfasalazine through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid interacts with willow bark through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of acebutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of alendronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of allopurinol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid increases the level or effect of amphetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the level or effect of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. A significant proportion of ciprofloxacin is excreted unchanged in the urine. When urinary alkalinizing agents like sodium citrate are used concomitantly, ciprofloxacin solubility may decrease due to alkaline urine, increasing the risk of crystalluria and nephrotoxicity. Patients should be monitored closely. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the level or effect of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Deferoxamine decreases the levels of sodium citrate or citric acid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor. Deferoxamine chelates iron, but its affinity for other minerals is unknown. Sodium citrate or citric acid decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
